title: repository.bootstrap registers the product in the manager catalog against paths that actually exist
description:
FILED BY worker-1d53e70c FROM task-80322112a48d44c69c6c55f846f8d43f (child 3, the browser proof), 2026-09-06 16:20Z, under SPIDR parent task-5ef1a0a9010c4bfe872ff9b774068234. task-80322112 dependsOn this row and is BLOCKED on it. The defect is in child 2's file (task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9, DONE and landed) - full finding with probe source and control in comment-710d0b5656154f07abaedd7273aa4508 on that row.

THE DEFECT, MEASURED NOT READ. `repository.bootstrap` CANNOT SUCCEED ON A REAL FILESYSTEM. Every local-only run reaches the last effect and answers BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED / CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED, after the repository has already been created, committed and BOUND. An operator is told the bootstrap failed while holding a perfectly good bound repository - the exact harm child 3 exists to prevent, arriving from a different direction.

WHERE. apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts:174-179 wires registerCatalog with configPath `${dir}/moe.config.json` and storePath `${dir}/.moe-next/store.sqlite`. NOTHING ON THE BOOTSTRAP PATH CREATES EITHER. `git grep -n "moe\.config\.json" apps/daemon/src` outside tests returns exactly two hits: cli/moe-init.ts:34 (names the constant) and :176 (consumes it). The controlled-profile scaffold emits neither (its set is package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.base.json, vite.config.ts, playwright.config.ts, docker-compose.yml, .gitignore, .env.example, README.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, migrations/, e2e/, packages/api/*, packages/web/*).

project-catalog.ts:127-140 canonicalEntry realpaths configPath and dirname(storePath); both ENOENT (root RESOLVES), so it refuses PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED; project-catalog-registrar.ts:67 THROWS it; repository-bootstrap-service.ts:66-67 catches a throwing port and answers BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED.

PROBE OUTPUT with a discriminating control (real registrar, node v24 type-stripping, probe deleted in the same call; full source in the child-2 comment):
  A_SCAFFOLD_SHAPED_INPUT: THREW ProjectCatalogRefusalError PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED
  CONTROL_PATHS_EXIST: REGISTERED_OK

WHY EVERY EXISTING ARM IS GREEN. repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:114 takes `Omit<RepositoryBootstrapSeams, "catalog">` and :127 stubs `catalog:` with an in-memory recorder, so the real createNodeProjectCatalogRegistrar and its realpath requirement are never exercised - including by :241 "SUCCEEDS local-only with gh absent: committed, bound, catalogued".

RECOMMENDED SHAPE, for the architect to confirm or overrule. Fix it in the composition at :174-179: create moe.config.json and .moe-next/ before registerCatalog, reusing cli/moe-init.ts which already knows the config format. NOT in the scaffold - moe.config.json and .moe-next are MOE's own project files, not files of the generated product. NOT in canonicalEntry - loosening the realpath contract weakens the catalog for every other caller and would let a typo register.

SCOPE: apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts plus its arms, and whatever cli/moe-init.ts must export to be reused. Small.
definitionOfDone: repository.bootstrap completes a local-only bootstrap against a REAL filesystem and a REAL catalog registrar: outcome BOOTSTRAPPED, refusal null, githubRefusal null, and the product present in the catalog file on disk. Asserted with the `catalog` seam NOT stubbed - a stub is precisely what hid this defect (repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:114,127).

The failing path keeps its stable code: when the catalog genuinely cannot be written (e.g. an unwritable catalog path), the receipt still answers BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED / CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED and the local repository is still retained. Assert the CODE, not merely that it refused, and name which layer refused.

A mutation drill proves the new arm is not vacuous: remove whatever now creates moe.config.json / .moe-next and confirm the arm reds with PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED reaching BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED. Restore proven by sha256 against an out-of-tree backup in a call separate from the restore (untracked paths are invisible to `git diff`).

The commit count is unchanged: a local-only bootstrap still leaves EXACTLY ONE commit in the new repository. Whatever writes moe.config.json / .moe-next must either land inside the single scaffold commit or be gitignored - `git log --oneline` = 1 line is task-80322112's DoD 2 and must not be broken by this fix.
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`. An exit-0 leg with no `Test Files N passed` count line ran nothing.
taskRails: THE LOCAL REPOSITORY IS ALREADY REAL WHEN THIS STEP RUNS. Bind has already succeeded. Never turn a catalog failure into a message that reads as total failure, and never delete or roll back the operator's committed repository to make a failure path tidy.

DO NOT LOOSEN `canonicalEntry` (project-catalog.ts:127-140). Its realpath contract protects every catalog caller from registering a path that does not exist; the bug is that bootstrap names paths it never creates, not that the catalog is too strict.
DO NOT STUB THE `catalog` SEAM IN THE ARM THAT PROVES THIS. The existing stub at repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:127 is the entire reason a command that can never succeed shipped green.
EXACTLY ONE COMMIT must remain in a freshly bootstrapped repository - task-80322112's Playwright journey asserts the LINE COUNT of `git log --oneline`, not merely that a commit exists.

implementationPlan.description:
**THE FIX.** `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts` (the composition at `:170-179`) and ONE line in `apps/daemon/src/repository/controlled-profile/controlled-profile-root-templates.ts`.

**CREATE `moe.config.json` AND `.moe-next/` BEFORE `registerCatalog` RUNS, AND AFTER `git.commit`.** The timing is the decision:
- **After the commit**, because `createBootstrapGitPort` runs `add -A` — creating them earlier would commit **`.moe-next/store.sqlite`, a SQLite database, into the operator's brand-new repository** (risk D).
- **Before `registerCatalog`**, because `canonicalEntry` realpaths `configPath` and `dirname(storePath)` and refuses `PROJECT_CATALOG_PATH_UNRESOLVED` if either is absent.

**ADD `.moe-next/` AND `moe.config.json` TO THE GENERATED `.gitignore`** (currently `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.env`, `*.log`, `playwright-report/`, `test-results/`). This is the one scaffold edit the row makes, and it is about what the product repo TRACKS rather than what the product IS — so it does not breach rail 3's "not in the scaffold".

**WHY THE CONFIG IS GITIGNORED RATHER THAN COMMITTED, and this is the call to overrule if the product disagrees:** `moe-init.ts:144-145` refuses `MOE_INIT_CONFIG_PRESENT` when `moe.config.json` is already in the target. A committed config would make `moe init` REFUSE on a fresh clone of that product. Write that reasoning into the code comment so the next reader can re-open it deliberately rather than by accident.

**REUSE `cli/moe-init.ts`'s CONSTANTS, NOT A COPY.** Import `MOE_CONFIG_FILENAME` and `MOE_CONFIG_SCHEMA_VERSION`; do not retype either literal. The file you write MUST parse back through `parseMoeConfig` — assert that in step 3 rather than trusting the shape.

**DO NOT TOUCH `canonicalEntry`** (rail 2) and **DO NOT ADD THESE TO THE CONTROLLED PROFILE'S FILE SET** (rail 3). The scaffold emits the product; these are Moe's own files.

**THE FAILING PATH IS UNCHANGED** (rail 1, DoD 2): when the catalog genuinely cannot be written the receipt still answers `BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED` / `CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED`, and the local repository is RETAINED. This row makes the success path reachable; it does not soften the failure path, and it never deletes the operator's repository to tidy one.

implementationPlan.description:
**THE ARMS — WITH THE `catalog` SEAM NOT STUBBED.** `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts`.

**(A) DoD 1 — A LOCAL-ONLY BOOTSTRAP SUCCEEDS END TO END** against a REAL filesystem and the REAL `createNodeProjectCatalogRegistrar`: `outcome: "BOOTSTRAPPED"`, `refusal: null`, `githubRefusal: null`, **and the product present in the catalog file on disk**. Read the catalog back from disk rather than trusting the registrar's return.

**THE SEAM MUST NOT BE STUBBED HERE** (rail 3, risk A). `:114` takes `Omit<RepositoryBootstrapSeams, "catalog">` and `:127` stubs it — that stub is why a command that can never succeed shipped green. This arm composes the real registrar. **`:241` ("SUCCEEDS local-only with gh absent: committed, bound, catalogued") currently asserts a success that cannot happen** — reconcile it: either point it at the real registrar too, or make its stubbed scope explicit in its name so it stops reading as proof of the thing it does not prove.

**(B) DoD 4 — EXACTLY ONE COMMIT.** `git log --oneline` in the new repository returns **exactly one line**. Assert the LINE COUNT, not that a commit exists — task-80322112's journey asserts the count and this fix must not break it.

**(C) THE STORE IS NOT COMMITTED.** `git ls-files` in the new repository contains **no `.moe-next/` path and no `moe.config.json`**, and `git status --porcelain` is CLEAN (both are gitignored). This is the arm that catches the timing mistake: create them before `add -A` and a database rides into the operator's first commit.

**(D) THE CONFIG PARSES BACK.** The written `moe.config.json` round-trips through `parseMoeConfig` (`moe-init.ts:191`) without refusal. A file that satisfies the catalog's realpath but is not a valid Moe config would pass (A) and be useless.

**(E) DoD 2 — THE FAILING PATH KEEPS ITS CODE.** With a genuinely unwritable catalog path, the receipt still answers `BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED` / `CATALOG_FAILED_LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED`, naming the layer that refused, **and the local repository is still on disk with its commit intact**. Assert the code and the retention, not merely that it refused.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 — THE ARMS, `catalog` SEAM NOT STUBBED. `repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts` 465 -> 670 lines. `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 19 passed (19)` (was 16; +3 arms). `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT 0.

THE SEAM IS UN-FENCED, WHICH IS THE STRUCTURAL FIX. `harness`'s parameter was `Omit<RepositoryBootstrapSeams, "catalog">` — it did not merely default to a recorder, it made reaching the production registrar TYPE-IMPOSSIBLE for every arm in the file. It is now `RepositoryBootstrapSeams`; the recorder is still the default (arms that do not care keep it) and an arm passing `catalog` REPLACES it, which the existing spread order already supported. A why-comment above `harness` records what the `Omit` cost, so nobody narrows it back for tidiness.

`realCatalog(catalogPath)` composes the REAL `createNodeProjectCatalogRegistrar` against a TEMP catalog path — the registrar takes its path as a parameter precisely so a test never touches `~/.moe-next/projects.json` (epic rail 4: no arm leaks outside its scratch dir, all of which are `rmSync`-ed by the existing `afterEach`). The wrapper only OBSERVES: it records the thrown `ProjectCatalogRefusalError`'s `code` and `layer` and rethrows the original untouched, so the command edge sees exactly what production sees. It does NOT reimplement any authority — it forwards `request` verbatim to the production registrar.

`catalogEntries(path)` reads the catalog FILE back off disk and parses it. DoD 1 asks for the product to be IN THE CATALOG; the registrar's return value would prove only that a promise resolved.

ARM (A) — DoD 1, "SUCCEEDS local-only against the REAL manager catalog: registered against paths that exist". `outcome: ACCEPTED`; durable receipt `outcome: BOOTSTRAPPED, refusal: null, githubRefusal: null`; `catalog.refusals` EMPTY; the catalog FILE ON DISK holds exactly one entry matching `{projectId, title}`; and both `moe.config.json` and `.moe-next` EXIST under the new dir. Adversarial detail asked for by step 4(d): the arm asserts `existsSync(dir) === false` BEFORE bootstrapping, so a pass cannot come from reusing a directory that happened to already have the right shape.

ARM (D) folded into (A) — the written config round-trips through `parseMoeConfig` with `expect(parsed.ok ? "PARSED" : parsed.code).toBe("PARSED")`, so a failure REPORTS THE REFUSAL CODE instead of `false !== true`. It then pins `projectId === PROJECT` and `storePath === join(dir, ".moe-next", "store.sqlite")` — i.e. the config and the catalog entry name the SAME store, which is the coupling that would silently rot. EPIC RAIL 3: the credential is asserted by WIDTH ONLY (`/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/`), never by value, and the arm additionally asserts the wire answer does not contain the string "credential".

ARM (B)+(C) — "leaves EXACTLY ONE commit and keeps moe.config.json and .moe-next OUT of it". `git log --oneline` LINE COUNT is 1 (task-80322112's DoD 2 pins the count, not the existence); `git ls-files` filtered for `.moe-next`/`moe.config.json` is EMPTY while still containing `.gitignore` (a positive control — an empty `ls-files` would satisfy the filter vacuously); `git status --porcelain` is CLEAN.
  **A VACUITY HOLE I FOUND AND CLOSED, worth flagging because the plan's drill 3 depended on it.** `writeMoeProjectFiles` creates `.moe-next/` but nothing inside it yet, and GIT CANNOT SEE AN EMPTY DIRECTORY. So a clean-tree assertion taken straight after bootstrap proves only that `moe.config.json` is ignored — deleting `.moe-next/` from the generated `.gitignore` would NOT have reddened it, and step 4's drill 3 would have been vacuous. The arm now writes a byte at the registered `storePath` (the exact state the daemon reaches when it opens that store on its next run) and re-asserts CLEAN plus one commit. That makes the `.moe-next/` line load-bearing rather than decorative, and drill 3 real.

ARM (E) — DoD 2, "keeps BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED and RETAINS the repository when the catalog cannot be written". The catalog path's PARENT is a FILE, so the registrar's `mkdir(dirname(path))` genuinely cannot succeed. I MEASURED that shape rather than assuming it (probe in %TEMP%, deleted): `PARENT_IS_FILE = ProjectCatalogRefusalError PROJECT_CATALOG_WRITE_FAILED layer= PROJECT_CATALOG`; the alternative shape `PATH_IS_DIR` yields `PROJECT_CATALOG_UNREADABLE`, a LOAD failure, so I did not use it — DoD 2 says "cannot be WRITTEN".
